To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a method to perform source-independent full wavefield elastic velocity analysis for surface seismic data, microseismic data, and vertical seismic profile data.
we developed a new source-independent full waveform elastic velocity analysis method for converted phase (CP) waves that does not require forward modeling and does not suffer from source aliasing.
(1) the method does not use source wavelet and can be applied to surface-seismic data; (2) it can also be applied to micro-seismic data; and (3) it is applicable to VSP studies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a source-independent full wavefield elastic velocity analysis technique that uses the converted phase elastic wavefield to improve the quality of P- and S-velocity models.
the development of new imaging and velocity analysis techniques for the analysis of elastic seismic data.
the development of a new approach to elastic velocity analysis that is based on the full waveform information of converted-phase elastic seismic signals, and does not use source wavelets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our method can be applied to surface-seismic and VSP studies to improve the resolution of P- and S- wave velocity estimates, and to microseismic data to obtain more accurate estimates of the location, origin time and mechanism of microseismic events.

the method presented in the manuscript is a novel approach to elastic velocity analysis that does NOT require source information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our approach is source-independent and is applicable to a broad spectrum of seismic studies.
we developed a source-independent full wavefield CP elastic migration velocity analysis approach for surface-seismic, teleseismics and VSP studies.
we present an approach to perform full waveform velocity analysis for CP elastic data that is applicable to a variety of geophysical applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of CP data can significantly improve the resolution of the velocity model and the quality of the migrated image, even with a small number of sources.
the proposed approach can be used to perform full waveform elastic velocity analysis using CP elastic data, and can be applied to surface-seismic surveys, teleseismic studies and VSPs.
CP elastic data can be used for imaging, and the method presented can be used to obtain accurate estimates of the P- and S-velocities from such data.
